# Introduction

Functions `extract_shell()` and `shell_script()` help with writing a shell script to control a data analysis workflow. `extract_shell()` and `shell_script()` do most of the work, but some additional editing is usually necessary.

# An example workflow

To demonstrate, we use a simple workflow where all the code, aside from the shell script, has already been written. The project directory contains the following files:

```{r, echo = FALSE}
dir_tree(regexp = nms_articles,
         invert = TRUE)
```

The workflow has five steps:

1. `src/cleaned_data.R` reads in the raw data, cleans it, and creates `out/cleaned_data.rds`
2. `src/model.R` fits a model to the cleaned data, and creates `out/model.rds`
3. `src/vals_fitted.R` extracts fitted values from the model, and creates `out/vals_fitted.rds`
4. `src/fig_fitted.R` uses `out/vals_fitted.rds` to create the plot in `out/fig_fitted.png`
5. `report.qmd` uses `out/fig_fitted.png` to create the document `report.html`

`cleaned_data.R`, `model.R`, and `vals_fitted.R`, and `fig_fitted.R` all contain calls to `cmd_assign()`. For instance, `src/model.R` contains the lines

```{r, echo = FALSE}
lines <- readLines("src/model.R")
cat(paste(c(lines[7:9], ""), collapse = "\n"))
```

# extract_shell()

`extract_shell()` extracts the call to `cmd_assign()` from an R file, and turns it into a shell command. For instance, the call

```{r, eval = FALSE}
extract_shell("src/model.R")
```
has return value
```{r, eval = TRUE, echo = FALSE}
extract_shell("src/model.R")
```

In the call to `cmd_assign()` above, the names `.cleaned_data` and `.out` start with a dot, and the name `rlm_method` does not. `extract_shell()` decides which arguments are file names in two steps. If the call includes any name that starts with a dot, those arguments are the file names, and the others are named arguments such as `--rlm_method=M`. If the call includes no dotted names, a value is treated as a file name when the file exists, or when the value looks like a path, such as when it contains a slash or ends with an extension such as `.csv`.

`extract_shell()` and `shell_script()` also read calls to `cmd_assign_collect()`. A character vector of paths becomes one file name per element, in the order written.

The easiest way to use `extract_shell()` is to call it from the R console, and then cut-and-paste the results into the shell script.


# shell_script()

`shell_script()` creates a draft of the whole shell script. `shell_script()` loops through all the R files in a directory, extracting `cmd_assign()` and `cmd_assign_collect()` calls and converting them into shell commands. It tries to put the commands in the order they need to run, by matching output paths with input paths, and then puts the commands into a script.

For instance, the call
<!-- Messages don't display properly, so don't print real output -->
```{r, eval = FALSE}
shell_script("src")
```
```{r, include = FALSE}
shell_script("src")
```
creates a new file called `workflow.sh` with the lines
```{r, echo = FALSE}
lines <- readLines("workflow.sh")
cat(paste(lines, collapse = "\n"))
```

`shell_script()` tries to put the commands in the order they need to run, by matching the path strings written in the calls. In this example the order is already right. It can get the order wrong, so the draft may still need editing. `shell_script()` also cannot see steps that are not R scripts. We add an instruction to render `report.qmd`.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
while (!nzchar(lines[[length(lines)]]))
  lines <- lines[-length(lines)]
lines <- c(lines,
	   "",
	   "quarto render report.qmd",
	   "")
cat(paste(lines, collapse = "\n"))
writeLines(lines, con = "workflow.sh")
```

# Running the shell script

Our project directory looks like this.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
dir_tree(regexp = nms_articles,
         invert = TRUE,
	 recurse = 1L)
```

We run the shell script.

```{bash}
bash workflow.sh
```

Our project directory now looks like this.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
dir_tree(regexp = nms_articles,
         invert = TRUE,
	 recurse = 1L)
```

We have created `cleaned_data.rds`, `model.rds`, and `vals_fitted.rds`, and `fig_fitted.png` in the `out` directory, and `report.html` in the main directory. The `report_files` directory was created by quarto.
